turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Right, sleeve up for me and I'll get your blood pressure before you go in.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, grand. I nearly turned around in the car park. It's a fuss over nothing.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is 122 over 76, pulse 86, temperature 36.5. You're all set.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thanks. Come on in and sit yourself down. What's been happening, in your own words?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah sure, a bit of spotting. Brown spots when I wipe. I'm grand — himself outside is the one losing the head.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): They often do. How long has the spotting been going on?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Since Saturday. Well, actually Saturday morning, so three days. It's light, not pouring.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any cramp, or pain low in the tummy, along with it?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): A small bit of cramp, low down, on and off the last day or two. It eases if I sit. I wouldn't even call it pain.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Have you any idea how far on you are? When was the last period?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, the last period was around Diwali, or after. I can't pin the day at all. Might be eight weeks, might be ten, I've no real idea.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's alright, we won't invent a date for it. Any clots, or bleeding heavy enough to soak a pad?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No clots, and nothing soaking a pad.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any dizziness, fainting, fever, or pain at the tip of the shoulder?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No, none of that. I'm a bit tired, but sure that's just the pregnancy.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tiredness is very common now. Are you taking any medicines at the moment?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Only folic acid, the pregnancy one from the chemist. Nothing else. I didn't even bother with a painkiller.
[SEG0018] person_1 (NURSE): Sorry to butt in, Doctor. The GP note on the chart says folic acid five milligrams once a day.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah no, that's wrong. Well, actually mine are the four hundred microgram tablets. I never took five milligrams.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fair enough, we won't guess between those two. Bring the box next time so we can read the packet. Any allergies you know of?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No allergies.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any illnesses behind you, or operations?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing at all. Never had an operation. I'm healthy.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke, or take a drink?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): I've never smoked. I was having the odd glass of wine, but I stopped once I knew I was pregnant.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Would you like your partner in? He's still outside.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): He can come in, yeah. He'll only wear out the floor otherwise. It's not that serious.
[SEG0028] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, I was pacing the corridor. She hardly slept last night with the worrying, even if she brushes it off.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): I slept badly, I'll give you that. And I'm a small bit anxious. I'm not in bits, though.

[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): A bit of worry is completely understandable. This could be a threatened miscarriage, or it could just be harmless spotting this early. I can't tell those apart yet, and the dates are too hazy to call.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Threatened — ah don't be saying that. It's a few spots, that's all.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): I hear you, and it may well be nothing serious. Still, I'd like a pelvic ultrasound today, and bloods for the pregnancy hormone, your blood group, and a full blood count.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Today? Um, well, if you really want. It'll be normal, I'd say.
[SEG0034] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We'll do them. I'd rather know, even if she's making little of it.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): The scan will be this afternoon, and the nurse can take the bloods now. Come back in to me once both are done and we'll go through them.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Back again this afternoon? I was dying to get home to the sofa. But grand, whatever you say.

[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the bleeding gets heavy, if the pain turns severe, or if you feel faint or you get shoulder pain, don't wait for this afternoon — come straight back, or go to the emergency department.
[SEG0038] person_1 (NURSE): I'll take those bloods next door now, and reception will send you down for the scan this afternoon.
